newsitem.title: USA: Countdown under way for U.S. space shuttle launch.
newsitem.headline: Countdown under way for U.S. space shuttle launch.

text.p: The countdown began on Monday for an 11-day space shuttle mission to probe Earth's upper atmosphere, observe a comet and test a Japanese robot arm.
Shuttle Discovery and its crew of six were due to blast off from Florida's Kennedy Space Centre at 10:41 a.m. EDT (1441 GMT) on Thursday .
NASA's traditional three-day countdown got under way on Monday afternoon, and space agency officials said there were no technical problems with the $2 billion reusable shuttle.
"Discovery is ready to go," shuttle commander Curt Brown said on Monday after arriving at the launch site with his crew.

U.S. Air Force meteorologists said there was a 40 percent chance bad weather could delay the shuttle's liftoff. An unusual midsummer cold front was expected to sweep into Florida on Thursday, bringing the threat of low clouds and rain.

Soon after going into orbit on Thursday, Discovery's crew is scheduled to release a German-built satellite to study Earth's upper atmosphere. The satellite will fly free of the shuttle for nine days before being retrieved.
The astronauts will also watch the receding Comet Hale-Bopp with a telescope through a shuttle cabin window and test a Japanese robot arm intended for use on the planned international space station.
